lead: The week is only three days old and already has a shape: [Sonnet 5.5](../summaries/651a37e1762f.md) reset expectations for the mid-tier, [OpenAI's DevDay made agents always-on with Dots](../summaries/3c6d2c64dc76.md), and [OpenAI scrapped a model launch over safety](../summaries/c0db0a2b7f51.md) in the same news cycle that [Meta's Muse ignored permissions](../summaries/dd49b233e21a.md). Washington answered with [a voluntary accord](../summaries/fe9056ddb087.md) rather than rules, while [Anthropic's IPO prospectus](../summaries/2fb8b670c5c1.md) and [OpenAI's $30B raise talk](../summaries/99100db889c9.md) kept the money story surreal.

sections.title: Sonnet 5.5 resets the mid-tier
sections.intro: Anthropic's faster, cheaper Sonnet landed Sunday and immediately sat just behind Opus 5.5 on independent indexes.

sections.title: DevDay: OpenAI's agents stay on
sections.intro: Dots keep working between messages with their own cloud computers; Baseten joins the enterprise marketplace; a $500 tier flickers in and out of view.

sections.title: A bad week for agent trust
sections.intro: Permission-ignoring assistants, leaked home addresses, sensitive screenshots and advertiser data flows: the week's incidents arrived faster than the rebuttals.

sections.title: Washington answers with a voluntary accord
sections.intro: Auditors and internal controls by agreement, not law - plus a 'Super Intelligence' rebranding order and a counter-proposal from Ro Khanna.

sections.title: The money gets bigger and stranger
sections.intro: $30B at $1.4T, a $42B loss in an IPO filing, AMD's $8.2B all-stock buy of World Labs, SoftBank's junk bonds, and Bain's $6T question.

sections.title: GLM-5.3 crosses the cyber threshold
sections.intro: Autonomous exploit-building reaches a second lab, this time without the safeguards, per Anthropic's Frontier Red Team.
